words.sense: unconventional, idiosyncratic, and departing harmlessly from standard social norms or routines
words.concise_meaning: deviating noticeably and harmlessly from customary character, convention, or social norms through peculiar individual habits or mannerisms
words.connotation: mildly amusing, colorful, nonconformist, harmlessly strange
words.grammar: adjective; can be used attributively ('an eccentric inventor') or predicatively ('her behavior is eccentric'); also functions as a countable noun ('an eccentric')
misconceptions: Assuming that any collection or combination of unusual items makes someone eccentric, confusing personal behavioral peculiarity with diverse stylistic gathering.

words.sense: selecting, combining, or composed of elements drawn from a wide variety of diverse sources or traditions
words.concise_meaning: deriving ideas, tastes, styles, or methods from a broad, varied, and heterogeneous range of independent sources
words.grammar: adjective; used attributively ('an eclectic mix', 'an eclectic taste') or predicatively ('the menu is eclectic')
misconceptions: Believing eclectic means weird, random, or socially bizarre, missing that it specifically signifies deliberate variety and breadth of originating sources.

semantic_axes.description: Personal idiosyncrasy deviating from social norms (eccentric) vs. breadth of origin drawing from diverse external traditions, genres, or disciplines (eclectic).
A singular, peculiar way of doing things centered on individual quirks (eccentric) vs. a composite mixture assembled by selecting from varied independent sources (eclectic).
Seen as odd, unconventional, or out of step with everyday expectations (eccentric) vs. seen as varied, wide-ranging, and culturally or intellectually diverse (eclectic).

edge.boundary_rule: Eccentric applies when behavior, personal habits, or thinking deviate strangely from conventional social norms; eclectic applies when an approach, taste, or collection draws together elements from a wide variety of distinct sources.
clues_a: following bizarre, self-invented personal routines with no cultural precedent
insisting on odd personal rituals that violate standard everyday etiquette
wearing standard items in nonsensical or peculiar ways out of personal idiosyncrasy
harmless fixations that isolate the actor from ordinary societal habits
refusing conventional conveniences in favor of strange personal superstitions
clues_b: deliberately combining elements from multiple distinct cultures, genres, or eras
curating a selection that spans unrelated intellectual disciplines or art movements
blending disparate traditions into a unified project or menu
drawing methods and insights from several competing schools of thought
displaying tastes that reject single-genre allegiance in favor of broad variety
irrelevant_clues: whether the person is wealthy, celebrated, or socially prominent
how loudly or quietly the action is performed
whether onlookers find the end result visually striking or unexpected
the total financial cost of the materials or habits involved

misconceptions.M1: Assuming any unusual or unconventional taste must be eccentric, overlooking that drawing intentionally from multiple diverse traditions makes it eclectic.
misconceptions.M2: Confusing a singular bizarre personal quirk with eclectic variety, failing to check whether multiple external sources are actually involved.
misconceptions.M3: Believing eclectic implies chaotic or disordered behavior, ignoring that eclectic properly denotes curated diversity from varied origins.

eccentric: The retired mathematics professor insisted on walking backward to the village market every morning while reciting prime numbers aloud.
Lord Harrington slept inside an open wooden coffin lined with velvet because he claimed beds trapped stale household air.
The village clockmaker refused paper money and only accepted payment in polished river stones of identical weight.
Miriam kept seven antique tea kettles boiling around her desk because she believed steam prevented negative thoughts from settling.
The wealthy recluse wore formal Victorian morning coats to the community swimming pool and greeted swimmers with a silver cane.
Old Mr. Gallagher spent every Tuesday afternoon tipping his bowler hat to the statues in the municipal park.
eclectic: The chef's tasting menu paired Mexican chipotle marinades with Japanese dashi broths and French pastry techniques.
Her personal bookshelf held medieval Icelandic sagas, modern cyberpunk novellas, and treatises on agricultural chemistry.
The festival program featured Appalachian bluegrass fiddlers, Ghanaian drumming ensembles, and electronic synthesizer pioneers.
His living room furniture combined mid-century Danish armchairs, Victorian carved tables, and bright handwoven Andean rugs.
The researcher's methodology borrowed survey techniques from sociology, statistical models from astrophysics, and field interviews from anthropology.
The band's debut album blended Delta blues slide guitar with Brazilian bossa nova rhythms and classical string arrangements.

eccentric: The university syllabus gathered essays from feminist theorists, Marxist economists, and neoclassical market analysts.
The interior decorator assembled contemporary Scandinavian lamps, antique Japanese screens, and rustic Italian pottery.
The diner ordered two scrambled eggs with white toast and black coffee, the standard breakfast she ate every morning.
The symphony orchestra performed Beethoven's Fifth Symphony strictly following the traditional tempo markings.
The disc jockey played a set mixing Chicago house, Jamaican dub, Punjabi bhangra, and Detroit techno.
The accountant filed her tax receipts in chronological order within standard labeled manila folders.
eclectic: The reclusive heiress ate all her meals while sitting atop a fifteen-foot stepladder in the center of her drawing room.
The museum exhibition displayed fifty oil paintings produced exclusively by Dutch landscape painters between 1640 and 1650.
The botanist only wore clothes made of unbleached yellow burlap because he believed dyed fabrics blocked solar energy.
The coffee shop served exclusively medium-roast Colombian drip coffee poured into identical white ceramic mugs.
The hermit insisted on entering every room through the window instead of using the front door.
The violinist practiced only Bach solo partitas for eight hours each day, refusing to listen to or play any other composer.

borderline.text: A neighborhood baker bakes his loaves using a medieval stone mill, decorates his shop with hubcaps, and delivers bread while riding a vintage penny-farthing bicycle.
borderline.note: Although multiple odd habits are on display, they do not form a systematic cross-cultural synthesis; rather, they reflect one individual's personal departure from conventional daily routines.

borderline.text: An architect designs a private villa featuring Moorish arched courtyards, Japanese cedar sliding screens, and Bauhaus steel-and-glass pavilions.
borderline.note: The structure draws directly and deliberately from three widely separated architectural traditions, making the design a classic example of multi-sourced synthesis.

borderline.text: A retired judge spends his afternoons tending a garden populated solely by carved stone gargoyles that he whispers to and tucks in with blankets.
borderline.note: The judge's behavior reflects deeply idiosyncratic, nonconformist personal conduct that departs harmlessly from conventional social habits without drawing on diverse traditions.
